Create a skill called btc-spot that fetches the current bitcoin USD price from coingecko (https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/simple/price?ids=bitcoin&vs_currencies=usd) and returns { price: <number> }. toolCalls.arguments:
{"repo": "skills", "goal": "Create a new skill called "btc-spot" in the skills repo.

Requirements:
- Directory: skills/btc-spot/ (or wherever this repo's convention places skill folders — follow existing skill examples in the repo for structure).
- Files: SKILL.md (manifest) and skill.py (entrypoint).

SKILL.md manifest:
- name: btc-spot
- description: Fetches the current Bitcoin spot price in USD from CoinGecko.
- tier: notify (no secrets, read-only network GET, no acting effects)
- effects: network read only
- network.allow: must include "api.coingecko.com"
- Do NOT declare any dependencies section.
- No inputs needed (skill takes no input parameters) — if an inputs section is required by convention for no-arg skills, represent it as taking no fields.

skill.py:
- Must define a single top-level async function `run` as the entrypoint, matching this repo's skill entrypoint convention (check existing skills in the repo for the exact signature pattern used, e.g. `async def run(inputs: Input, ctx: Ctx) -> Output` with pydantic models imported from `cogmo_ctx`, or a plain two-parameter signature — mirror whatever the repo's existing skills do).
- Fetch url = "https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/simple/price?ids=bitcoin&vs_currencies=usd" using `await ctx.http.get(url)` ONLY. Do NOT use urllib, requests, httpx, or any other HTTP library.
- The ctx.http.get call returns a dict with keys 'status' and 'body'. Parse the 'body' value with `json.loads(...)` to get the JSON data.
- Extract the bitcoin USD price from the parsed JSON (structure: {"bitcoin": {"usd": <number>}}).
- Return an object/dict equivalent to `{ "price": <number> }` — if the repo convention uses a pydantic Output model, define `class Output` with a single field `price: float` (or int/float as appropriate) and return an instance of it; if plain dict return is the convention, return `{"price": price}`.
- Do NOT create a requirements.lock file or declare any third-party dependencies anywhere.
- Handle a non-200 status from ctx.http.get by raising a clear error (do not silently fail).

Please look at an existing skill in this repo first to match the exact conventions for folder layout, SKILL.md fields/format, and skill.py entrypoint signature before writing the new files, so this skill is consistent with the others."}
